q01.q: What's the full address of the house, and roughly when did you buy it?
q01.why: Anchors the whole record and the future buyer handoff package.

q02.q: Year built, square footage, bedrooms and bathrooms — whatever you know offhand.
q02.why: Rough is fine. If you have the listing sheet, attach it instead.

q03.q: Do you have the home inspection report or closing documents from the purchase? If so, attach them.
q03.why: These usually list the age of the roof, HVAC and water heater — they can answer a dozen questions at once.

q04.q: HVAC: how many units, what brand, roughly how old, and who services them?
q04.why: A photo of each unit's data plate — on the furnace and the outdoor condenser — gives the model and serial numbers.

q05.q: When was the HVAC last serviced, and do you have a maintenance plan with anyone?
q05.why: Sets the last-done to next-due clock for the seasonal tune-ups.

q06.q: Water heater: tank or tankless, gas or electric, and roughly how old?
q06.why: A data-plate photo works here too.

q07.q: Roof: how old is it, and when was it last replaced or repaired?
q07.why: One of the first things a buyer asks about.

q08.q: Have the windows or exterior doors been replaced? If so, when, by whom, and what did it cost?
q08.why: Attach the contract or warranty certificate if you have it — only what the paperwork says gets recorded.

q09.q: Garage doors and openers: brand, roughly how old, and have they been replaced?
q09.why: Openers and doors carry separate warranties, so both are worth recording.

q10.q: Where are the main water shutoff, the gas shutoff and the electrical panel?
q10.why: Property knowledge a house sitter, contractor or future owner needs in a hurry.

q11.q: Anything unusual about the plumbing or electrical — old pipes, a subpanel, a generator, known quirks?
q11.why: Lessons learned from past repairs belong in the record, not in your head.

q12.q: Who services the pool, and what does that cost? When was the equipment last serviced or replaced?
q12.why: Pump, heater and filter each have their own age and warranty.

q13.q: Who handles the irrigation system, and when is it started up and winterized?
q13.why: Start-up and blowout are seasonal dates worth putting on the clock.

q14.q: Septic or well: who services it, how often, and when was it last pumped or tested?
q14.why: Both run on strict intervals that are easy to lose track of.

q15.section: People who work on the house
q15.q: Who is your cleaning person — name, phone, which days they come, and what you pay?
q15.why: Sets up the weekly cleaning priorities list and the payment record.

q16.section: People who work on the house
q16.q: Who handles lawn and landscaping, and pest control? Company, contact, how often, and cost.
q16.why: Recurring providers go in the directory with their payment schedule.

q17.section: People who work on the house
q17.q: Any other go-to people — plumber, electrician, handyman, HVAC company, painter? Include anyone you've used before, even if you've switched.
q17.why: Former providers stay in the record with the work they did.

q18.q: Kitchen and laundry appliances: brands and roughly when purchased? Photos of the model and serial stickers are perfect.
q18.why: Fridge, range, dishwasher, microwave, washer, dryer.

q19.q: Do you know the paint colors — brand and color name — for the main rooms and the exterior?
q19.why: Saves a paint-store guessing game at touch-up time and goes in the sale package.

q20.q: Flooring: what's where, and when was any of it installed or replaced?
q20.why: Affects cleaning as well as the record.

q21.q: Is anything broken, overdue, or bugging you about the house right now?
q21.why: Becomes the first entries in what needs to happen.

q22.q: Anything planned in the next year — a project, a replacement you know is coming, a room you want redone?
q22.why: Projects get tracked from idea through completion.
